title: Paper Submission Readiness Checklist — All 3 Papers
summary: Comprehensive submission readiness evaluation for three papers: leverage-direction (JBF target), taiwan-vt (PBFJ target), vt-trend-following (target TBD).

papers.title: Leverage Direction Matters: Cross-Asset Evidence on GARCH Model Selection and Volatility Targeting
papers.journal_page_limit: ~50-60 pages (double-spaced, JBF has no strict limit but 40-50 main text + appendices is typical)
papers.page_assessment: At 64 pages, slightly above typical JBF length. Could benefit from trimming appendices or moving some robustness to supplementary material. The appendices (Commodity Extension, TZ Arbitrage, Practical Summary) add ~10 pages that could be online-only.
papers.tables_figures_assessment: 14 tables and 6 figures is substantial but within JBF norms for a comprehensive empirical paper. All 6 figure PDFs exist on disk.
papers.references_assessment: 47 references is reasonable for JBF. All bibitems in main.tex are referenced in body.tex via inline author-year citation style (e.g., 'Bollerslev (1986)' rather than \citet{}). No missing citation keys detected.

k_numbers_in_knowledge.K477: referenced in comment only, not formal K-number in text

papers.k_numbers_assessment: All K-numbers are used only in LaTeX comments (% K486/K490: ...) for internal tracking, not visible in compiled PDF. All exist in knowledge.json.
papers.correction_notices: None found. No warning/correction notices in the paper.

abstract.assessment: Abstract is well-structured with three clear contributions, specific statistics (gamma values, Spearman rho, DM results), and appropriate scope. Mentions extended OOS (2026 Iran crisis). Keywords and JEL codes present.

conclusion.assessment: Conclusion properly reflects all three contributions. HAR paradox (K530) is discussed in Section 5.8 and referenced in the complexity ceiling table. VIX-conditional leverage (K548) is covered in Section 5.6. The conclusion accurately summarizes: (1) leverage direction taxonomy, (2) gamma-mechanism proposition with domain boundaries, (3) TZ information transmission with c2c/o2o distinction.

papers.title: Volatility Targeting in the Taiwan Stock Market: Leverage Amplification, Model Selection, and Practical Implementation
papers.page_assessment: 38 pages is within PBFJ norms. The paper covers three substantial topics (leverage amplification, VT strategies, TZ info transmission) which justifies the length.
papers.tables_figures_assessment: 6 tables and 0 figures. The absence of figures is a notable gap — PBFJ papers typically include at least 2-3 figures. Missing: rolling gamma chart, VT cumulative returns chart, overnight gap visualization. This should be addressed before submission.
papers.references_assessment: Only 16 references — this is THIN for PBFJ. Missing several key citations that should be added: Chevallier & Ielpo (2017) for commodity leverage, Corsi (2009) for HAR, Hansen & Lunde (2005) for GARCH comparison, Moskowitz et al. (2012) for TSMOM. Also missing: barndorff2010 (cited in text but no bibitem).

papers.k_numbers_assessment: All K-numbers are used in LaTeX comments only (not visible in compiled output). All exist in knowledge.json with matching content.

abstract.assessment: Abstract is comprehensive but LONG (~420 words). PBFJ typically expects ~150-250 words. Should be condensed significantly — currently tries to cover all findings including macro indicators, TSMC decomposition, and conditional leverage. Focus on the 3 core contributions.

conclusion.assessment: Conclusion properly covers: (1) leverage amplification with TAIEX vs 0050.TW distinction, (2) VT strategy comparison with QLIKE-VT disconnect, (3) TZ info transmission with c2c/o2o gap. Limitations are well-stated including VIXTWN data limitation, TSMC concentration risk, and single-market scope.

papers.title: Is Volatility Targeting Just Trend Following? Decomposing the Benefits of Volatility Targeting
papers.journal_suggestions: Journal of Portfolio Management (JPM — most natural fit given VT/TSMOM content and Hood & Raughtigan 2025 reference), Journal of Financial Economics (JFE — stretch target), Financial Analysts Journal (FAJ)
papers.page_assessment: 26 pages is compact for the scope covered (22-asset analysis, international evidence, 5 factor models). Appropriate for JPM or FAJ. If targeting JFE, would need expansion.
papers.tables_figures_assessment: 5 tables (alpha decomposition, cross-section, dual mechanism, FF5, international) and 0 figures. The absence of figures is a gap — at minimum should include: gamma vs TSMOM loading scatter plot, MDD decomposition bar chart, international VT protection heatmap.
papers.references_assessment: 18 references is adequate for a focused 26-page paper. 3 bibitems are uncited: barroso2015, daniel2016, fleming2001 — should either cite them in text or remove from bibliography. Key references are present (Moreira & Muir, Hood & Raughtigan, Moskowitz et al., Harvey et al.).
papers.k_numbers_assessment: All K-numbers are in LaTeX comments only. All exist in knowledge.json.

abstract.assessment: Abstract is excellent — clear 3-contribution structure, specific numbers (90-97% MDD retention, r=0.564, 13/13 markets), and precise conclusion (VT as drawdown insurance priced at ~4%/year). Length appropriate for most journals.

conclusion.assessment: Conclusion covers: (1) gamma predicts TSMOM loading, (2) dual mechanism (Sharpe vs MDD), (3) 12/VIX irreducibility, (4) international evidence. References K568 findings (12/VIX return-optimal) and K518 (trend-following strategies fail Harvey). Well-structured with 4 practical implications.
